This page documents the current **[Minecraft Forge](https://minecraftforge.net/) protocol**, including how to connect to servers running Minecraft Forge and what changes it makes to the vanilla protocol.

# FML protocol (1.7 - 1.12)

Largely based off of [Pokechu22's work on getting Minecraft Console Client to connect to Forge servers](https://github.com/ORelio/Minecraft-Console-Client/pull/100), this section describes the FML protocol used for Minecraft 1.7.X to 1.12.X.

## Changes to [Server List Ping](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Server_List_Ping?action=edit&redlink=1 "Server List Ping (page does not exist)")

When forge is installed, the [Server List Ping](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Server_List_Ping?action=edit&redlink=1 "Server List Ping (page does not exist)") changes with additional mod information:

```
{
    "description": "A Minecraft Server",
    "players": {
        "max": 20,
        "online": 0
    },
    "version": {
        "name": "1.8",
        "protocol": 47
    },
    "modinfo": {
        "type": "FML",
        "modList": [
            {
                "modid": "mcp",
                "version": "9.05"
            },
            {
                "modid": "FML",
                "version": "8.0.99.99"
            },
            {
                "modid": "Forge",
                "version": "11.14.3.1512"
            },
            {
                "modid": "rpcraft",
                "version": "Beta 1.3 - 1.8.0"
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

So, to test whether forge is installed, look for the `modinfo` key and then a `type` of `FML`

The `modList` contains each installed mod's version and ID.

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

The key `modList` has a capital 'L', unlike any other key in the ping result!

This is injected in [ServerStatusResponse](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/patches/minecraft/net/minecraft/network/ServerStatusResponse.java.patch#L45) by calling [FMLNetworkHandler.enhanceStatusQuery()](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/internal/FMLNetworkHandler.java#L197-L211).

## Connection to a forge server

Attempting to connect to a forge server without making any changes results in getting immediately disconnected with the message "`This server requires FML/Forge to be installed. Contact your server admin for more details.`". This message is displayed in [FMLCommonHandler](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/FMLCommonHandler.java#L653-L661) and is [injected](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/patches/minecraft/net/minecraft/network/handshake/client/C00Handshake.java.patch#L35) in a modified [0x00 Handshake packet](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Handshake "Protocol").

If `\0FML\0` is added to the end of the server's address (where `\0` is a [Wikipedia:null character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/null_character "wikipedia:null character")) (again, in the 0x00 handshake packet), the server will not immediately reject you. However, you still will not complete the connection.

This occurs because Minecraft Forge has an additional set of handshakes (for determining mods and block IDs), that must be completed before the server allows logging in.

## Forge handshake

Forge's handshake occurs in the middle of the [normal login sequence](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol_FAQ?action=edit&redlink=1 "Protocol FAQ (page does not exist)"), right after [0x02 Login Success](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Success "Protocol") is received by the client.

In addition to the [normal packet debugging](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Debugging?action=edit&redlink=1 "Debugging (page does not exist)") for the server, if `-Dfml.debugNetworkHandshake=true` is passed to the forge server, some more information about the current handshake status will be outputted.

[Template:Need Info](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Need_Info?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Need Info (page does not exist)")

- **S→C**: [`REGISTER`](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") forge's plugin channels: FML|HS, FML, FML|MP, FML, FORGE (yes, FML is there twice; technically, it does not need to be there twice but that is the way that Forge sends it and sending it that way will act more similar to forge)
- **S→C**: A ServerHello packet is sent on `FML|HS` including the player's dimension (0 if it's the first login)
- **C→S**: `REGISTER` the plugin channels: FML|HS, FML, FML|MP, FML, FORGE.
- **C→S**: A ClientHello packet is sent on the `FML|HS` channel.
- **C→S**: A ModList packet is sent.
- Server checks that the mod list is compatible. If incompatible, the player is [disconnected](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Disconnect "Protocol") with an explanatory message. Otherwise, continue.
- **S→C**: A ModList packet is sent.
- Client checks that the mod list is compatible. If incompatible, it disconnects. Otherwise, continue.
- **C→S**: A HandshakeAck packet is sent, with the phase being `WAITINGSERVERDATA` (2).
- **S→C**: A series of RegistryData packets is sent, with hasMore being true for all packets except the last.
- Client reads and stores each RegistryData, continuing reading until hasMore is false. Once hasMore is false, it checks whether it has all of the needed blocks/items. If it does not, it disconnects. Otherwise, continue.
- **C→S**: A HandshakeAck packet is sent with phase being `WAITINGSERVERCOMPLETE` (3).
- **S→C**: A HandshakeAck packet is sent with phase being `WAITINGCACK` (2).
- **C→S**: A HandshakeAck packet is sent with phase being `PENDINGCOMPLETE` (4).
- **S→C**: A HandshakeAck packet is sent with phase being `COMPLETE` (3).
- The server sends a "CompleteHandshake" packet **to itself**. (Not sure why)
- **C→S**: A HandshakeAck packet is sent with phase being `COMPLETE` (5).
- The client sends a "CompleteHandshake" packet **to itself**. (Not sure why)

## Definitions

Minecraft Forge uses an additional type not covered in [data types](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Data_types "Data types") for some things -- a varshort. This is essentially the same as a regular short, except that if the top byte (what is normally sign) is set, it is followed by an additional byte. This allows forge to retain backwards compatibility but extend the length of certain numbers -- the varshort is only used in places where, in vanilla Minecraft, the sign bit would not have been set. It is implemented in [ByteBufUtils](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/ByteBufUtils.java#L58-L89).

Discriminator bytes are the way that Minecraft Forge allows sending multiple messages on one [plugin channel](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)"). They aren't part of the original specification, but a similar concept is used with the [`MC|AdvCdm` plugin channel](https://wiki.vg/index.php?title=Plugin_channels&oldid=14089#MC.7CAdvCmd) (used for command blocks). That packet decides whether a block location is being sent or an entity ID (minecart command blocks) is being sent based off of the value of the first byte in the packet.

In the same way, forge uses the first byte of the plugin message to specify which packet to use. It uses [FMLIndexedMessageToMessageCodec](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/FMLIndexedMessageToMessageCodec.java) to automatically switch the value.

Discriminator bytes change depending on the channel: 0 for `FML|HS` means something different from 0 for `FML`.

## `FML|HS` Packet structure

`FML|HS` is used to perform the handshake. Discriminator bytes are found in [FMLHandshakeCodec](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeCodec.java).

### [ServerHello](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeMessage.java#L33-L76)

Starts the handshake.

| Channel | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|HS` | Client | Discriminator | Byte | Always 0 for ServerHello |
| FML protocol Version | Byte | Determined from [NetworkRegistery](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/NetworkRegistry.java#L67-L69). Currently `2`. |
| Override dimension | Optional Int | Only sent if protocol version is greater than 1. |

### [ClientHello](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeMessage.java#L77-L95)

Response from the client to the ServerHello packet.

| Channel | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|HS` | Server | Discriminator | Byte | Always 1 for ClientHello. |
| FML protocol Version | Byte | Determined from [NetworkRegistery](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/NetworkRegistry.java#L67-L69). Currently `2`. |

### [ModList](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeMessage.java#L96-L152)

Contains a list of all mods installed on the server or client. Sent from the client to the server first, and then the server responds with its mod list. The server's mod list matches the one sent in the ping.

| Channel | Bound To | Field Name | | Field Type | | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|HS` | Both | Discriminator | | Byte | | Always 2 for ModList |
| Number of mods | | Varint | | Number of mods below |
| Mods | Mod name | Array | String | Name of the mod |
| Mod version | String | Version of the mod |

### [RegistryData](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/6e90348dc546164b21735aefd83ed0bac0d8283c/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeMessage.java#L154-L240)

[Template:Need Info](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Need_Info?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Need Info (page does not exist)")

The server sends several of this packet, one for each registry. It'll keep sending them until the hasMore value is no longer true.

| Channel | Bound To | Field Name | | Field Type | | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|HS` | Both | Discriminator | | Byte | | Always 3 for RegistryData. |
| Has more | | Boolean | | Marks whether another RegistryData packet will be sent after this. |
| Name | | String | | Name of the registry for this packet |
| Number of ids | | Varint | | Number of ids sent below |
| Ids | Name | Array | String | Name of the thing |
| Id | Varint | Numerical id of the thing |
| Number of substitutions | | Varint | | Number of substitutions sent below |
| Substitutions | | Array of strings | | Each substitution |
| Number of dummies | | Varint | | Number of dummies in the array below. **May not be present in older versions of forge**; check if there still is data remaining in the packet before continuing to read data. |
| Dummies | | Array of strings | | Each dummy? |

### [HandshakeAck](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeMessage.java#L241-L264)

Confirms that the client is able to use the settings sent previously.

| Channel | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|HS` | Both | Discriminator | Byte | Always -1 (255) for HandshakeAck |
| Phase | Byte | The current phase, which is the ordinal (0-indexed) in the [FMLHandshakeClientState](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeClientState.java) or [FMLHandshakeServerState](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeServerState.java) enums (if the server is sending it, it is in the ServerState enum, and if the client is sending it, it is the ClientState enum). |

### [HandshakeReset](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeMessage.java#L265-L267)

Causes the client to recomplete the entire handshake from the start. There is no payload beyond the discriminator byte.

The normal forge server does not ever use this packet, but it is used [when connecting through a BungeeCord instance](https://github.com/SpigotMC/BungeeCord/blob/aaddc9fcfdcada8d19ab115f2dcc8aed413a9206/proxy/src/main/java/net/md_5/bungee/ServerConnector.java#L126-L138), specifically when transitioning from a vanilla server to a modded one or from a modded server to another modded server.

| Channel | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|HS` | Client | Discriminator | Byte | Always -2 (254) for HandshakeReset |

## `FML|MP` and multipart packets

Forge supports splitting large clientbound plugin message packets into smaller multipart packets. This functionality does not exist serverbound. This system is available in all versions.

This system starts by [sending](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/16bfd8cef1d12ee9ca0de1122addaf9916767ae9/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/internal/FMLProxyPacket.java#L164-L167) an `FML|MP` packet to indicate what the actual packet is (note that this is within the plugin message itself):

| Channel | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|MP` | Client | Channel | String (20) | The wrapped channel |
| Parts | Unsigned byte | Total number of parts (equal to `ceil(dataLength / (double)(1048495))` |
| Length | Int | Total length of wrapped data |

This is [followed](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/16bfd8cef1d12ee9ca0de1122addaf9916767ae9/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/internal/FMLProxyPacket.java#L173-L178) by a series of additional `FML|MP` packets which write the payload. Each packet is prefixed with the part number as an unsigned byte (starting at 0), followed by the rest of the packet containing up to 1048495 bytes of the actual message. Each packet must be sent in order.

Up to 52424750 bytes (~52 megabytes) may be sent through this system.

## Differences from Forge 1.7.10

Forge for Minecraft 1.8 made some changes from the 1.7.10 version.

The most important thing to keep track of isn't (entirely) a forge change. In 1.7.10, [plugin channel packets](http://wiki.vg/index.php?title=Protocol&oldid=6003#Plugin_Message_2) are length prefixed, while in 1.8 they are not. However, forge makes [some more changes](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/605457deecba2144d69113d3c9ce6589021f542b/fml/patches/minecraft/net/minecraft/network/play/server/S3FPacketCustomPayload.java.patch) to the server to client packet (but not the client to server packet): Rather than using a short for the length, a varshort is used. Due to the way that varshorts work, this is backwards compatible, but if this is not accounted for you may receive forge packets that seem corrupted as there is an extra byte that appears seemingly randomly.

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

While it may seem like you can get away with not handling varshorts, on servers with lots of mods (EG FTB), this will appear.

Additionally, in 1.7.10 the registries packet is instead "ModIdData":

### [ModIdData](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/ebe9b6d4cbc4a5281c386994f1fbda04df5d2e1f/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/common/network/handshake/FMLHandshakeMessage.java#L154-L240)

Contains numeric ID mapping for blocks and items.

[Template:Need Info](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Need_Info?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Need Info (page does not exist)")

| Channel | Bound to | Name | | Type | | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FML|HS` | Client | Discriminator | | Byte | | Always 3 for ModIdData |
| Mapping length | | VarInt | | Length of the following mapping |
| Mapping | Name | Array | String | Name of the block/item. Prefixed with a [discriminator byte](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/1.7.10/fml/src/main/java/cpw/mods/fml/common/registry/GameData.java#L763-L766), 01 = block, 02 = item. |
| ID | VarInt | Numeric ID of the item. |
| Block substitutions length | | VarInt | | Length of the following array |
| Block substitutions | | Array of strings | | Block substitutions |
| Item substitutions length | | VarInt | | Length of the following array |
| Item substitutions | | Array of strings | | Item substitutions |

# FML2 protocol (1.13 - Current)

This section is also mostly based off [research on making Minecraft Console Client join 1.13+ Forge servers](https://github.com/ORelio/Minecraft-Console-Client/commit/a28409043ca66f811103e2cd57a6b8130baf7768#diff-8ecd732a672d36828f2451352c312eb7R243). As a result, it only describes the necessary steps for joining a Forge server, but not all its network protocol.

## Changes to [Server List Ping](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Server_List_Ping?action=edit&redlink=1 "Server List Ping (page does not exist)")

When forge is installed, the [Server List Ping](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Server_List_Ping?action=edit&redlink=1 "Server List Ping (page does not exist)") changes with additional mod information. Example for 1.13.2:

```
{
  "description": {
    "text": "A Minecraft Server"
  },
  "players": {
    "max": 20,
    "online": 0
  },
  "version": {
    "name": "1.13.2",
    "protocol": 404
  },
  "forgeData": {
    "channels": [
      {
        "res": "ironchest:main_channel",
        "version": "1",
        "required": false
      }
    ],
    "mods": [
      {
        "modId": "forge",
        "modmarker": "ANY"
      },
      {
        "modId": "ironchest",
        "modmarker": "1.13.2-8.0.2"
      }
    ],
    "fmlNetworkVersion": 2
  }
}
```

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

The key `modId` has a capital 'I', unlike `modid` pre-1.13

for the previous FML protocol.

## Changes to [Handshake](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Handshake "Protocol") packet

Forge adds a marker to the `Server Address` field of the [Handshake](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Handshake "Protocol") packet: `\0FML2\0` is added to the end of the server's address, where `\0` is a [null character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Null_character). Unless the Forge server has no mods installed, attempting to connect to a Forge server without making any changes results in getting immediately disconnected with the message `This server has mods that require Forge to be installed on the client. Contact your server admin for more details.`. Inferring the correct marker to use is possible by examining the Server List Ping response from the server. FML2 will set the `forgeData` > `fmlNetworkVersion` to `2`.

*References:*

- [FMLNetworkConstants.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/638d1d31deabd8a83cf4b84496549703bc527ab4/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLNetworkConstants.java#L37): `FML2` marker
- [NetworkHooks.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/638d1d31deabd8a83cf4b84496549703bc527ab4/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/NetworkHooks.java#L57): Get marker from server IP
- [FMLHandshakeHandler.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/638d1d31deabd8a83cf4b84496549703bc527ab4/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeHandler.java#L116): Get connection type from maker
- [ServerLifecycleHooks.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/server/ServerLifecycleHooks.java#L165): Reject vanilla clients on mising marker

## Handshake Protocol

After receiving the [Login Start](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Start "Protocol") packet, the Forge server communicates with the Forge client using [Login Plugin Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Plugin_Request "Protocol") and [Login Plugin Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Plugin_Response "Protocol") packets before allowing the vanilla login phase to proceed as usual. Each packet must be understood and replied accordingly by the client, or the login attempt is rejected with a [Disconnect (Login)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Disconnect_.28login.29 "Protocol") packet.

### Login Wrapper

As per [FMLLoginWrapper.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/638d1d31deabd8a83cf4b84496549703bc527ab4/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLLoginWrapper.java), the [Login Plugin Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Plugin_Request "Protocol") and [Login Plugin Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Plugin_Response "Protocol") are formatted as follows:

- `Channel` is `fml:loginwrapper`
- `Data` has the following layout:

| Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Channel | Identifier | Name of the plugin channel. `fml:handshake` for FML handshake. |
| Inner Packet | [Packet](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Packet_format "Protocol") | Same layout as vanilla packets. Forge [uses Minecraft's PacketBuffer class](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/638d1d31deabd8a83cf4b84496549703bc527ab4/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLLoginWrapper.java#L59) to decode the packet. |

### Handshake Channel

Packets exchanged on the `fml:handshake` channel are described below. As per [Login Plugin Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Plugin_Request "Protocol") and [Login Plugin Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Login_Plugin_Response "Protocol") requirements, each request sent by the server expects exactly one packet back from the client, wrapped as described in [Login Wrapper](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)"). The client can only respond to requests from the server. The FML handshake completes successfully once the client has correctly responded to all requests from the server.

*References:*

- [NetworkInitialization.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/NetworkInitialization.java): Packet IDs
- [FMLHandshakeMessages.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeMessages.java): Packet layouts
- [FMLHandshakeHandler.java](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeHandler.java): Packet handling code

#### [Mod List](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeMessages.java#L63)

Advertises the list of Mods, [Plugin channel](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") and Registries on the Forge server.

| Packet ID | Bound To | Field Name | | Field Type | | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Client | Mod Count | | VarInt | | Length of the Mods array |
| Mod Names | | Array of String | | List of Mods installed on the Server |
| Channel Count | | VarInt | | Length of the Channels array |
| Channels | Name | Array | Identifier | Name of the [Plugin channel](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") |
| Marker | String | Version of the [Plugin channel](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") |
| Registry Count | | VarInt | | Length of the Registries array |
| Registries | | Array of Identifier | | List of Registries on the Server |

The client is supposed to check the list of mods against its own list, and [abort login if a mismatch is detected](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeHandler.java#L178). Otherwise, it should reply with [Mod List Reply](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)") to continue the handshake process.

#### [Mod List Reply](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeMessages.java#L131)

Advertises the list of Mods, [Plugin channels](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channels?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channels (page does not exist)") and Registries on the Forge client, in reply to [Mod List](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)").

| Packet ID | Bound To | Field Name | | Field Type | | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | Server | Mod Count | | VarInt | | Length of the Mods array |
| Mod Names | | Array of String | | List of Mods installed on the Server |
| Channel Count | | VarInt | | Length of the Channels array |
| Channels | Name | Array | Identifier | Name of the [Plugin channel](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") |
| Marker | String | Version of the [Plugin channel](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") |
| Registry Count | | VarInt | | Length of the Registries array |
| Registries | Name | Array | Identifier | Name of the registry |
| Marker | String | Version of the registry |

Compared to [Mod List](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)"), this packet also includes a Marker for each Registry. As of MC 1.16, the Forge server [only checks the contents of the mod list](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeHandler.java#L202), so a client just wanting to pass the server-side check can reply with the data provided by the server and leave an empty string in the Registry Marker field.

#### [Server Registry](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeMessages.java#L212)

Advertises a registry to the client. The Forge server will send one request/packet per registry.

[Template:Need Info](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Need_Info?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Need Info (page does not exist)")

| Packet ID | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | Client | Registry Name | Identifier | Name of the registry |
| Snapshot Present | Boolean | Indicates if a Snapshot is present |
| Snapshot | [Forge Snapshot](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/registries/ForgeRegistry.java#L812) | Snapshot of the registry |

A client is expected to process the registry and reply with an [Acknowledgement](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)") packet.

#### [Configuration Data](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeMessages.java#L252)

Advertises configuration data to the client.

| Packet ID | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | Client | File Name | String | Name of the configuration file |
| Data | Array of Bytes | File contents (may be a String) |

A client is expected to process the configuration data and reply with an [Acknowledgement](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)") packet.

#### [Acknowledgement](https://github.com/MinecraftForge/MinecraftForge/blob/fe43088c96cf65c6793260eae96416871a9eb8f2/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/network/FMLHandshakeMessages.java#L202)

Acknowledges a [Server Registry](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)") or [Configuration Data](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Forge_Handshake?action=edit&redlink=1 "Minecraft Forge Handshake (page does not exist)") packet.

| Packet ID | Bound To | Field Name | Field Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 99 | Server |  |  |  |

This is a dummy packet sent back when no reply payload is required, as each request sent by the server expects a packet back from the client.
